propositions: The snapshot janitor's free-space trigger uses an absolute 2 GiB floor that is disk-size-blind, crossing only at 93.3% used on a 30 GiB root, which sits above both the 85% alarm threshold and the 90% peak observed, making the trigger unreachable before alarming.

Root disk usage climbed from 71% to 90% in ~1 hour at 4.4 GiB/h because every review materializes a fresh ~620 MiB copy of the ticket tree (~70k files) keyed on a tip advancing every ~26 seconds, with nearly zero reuse of cache entries.

The snapshot store sits on the container writable layer (30 GiB root) instead of a separate volume because REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR is unset everywhere, causing store_root() to fall through to tempfile.gettempdir() on the root disk.

The 90% peak reclaim (12.6 GiB drop to 48% floor) is caused by container recreation destroying the entire writable layer, not by Docker prune, as evidenced by 23 independent reclaim events all landing on the identical 48% floor and occurring immediately after BOT_PATHS commits.

The 7-day cold-trim eviction trigger is dead code because the container is recreated every ~4 hours, and the byte-total backstop promised by ADR 0005 and the module docstring is not implemented in _gc_pass, leaving only the unreachable absolute watermark as a live trigger.

Making the janitor's reclaim threshold volume-relative by adding a percentage-based term allows it to engage before the alarm floor on small volumes, with hysteresis to overshoot the trigger rather than re-fire every 300 seconds.
